questions.solution:
Given:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}=57 \mathrm{meV}=57 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{ J}\\
& \mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\\
& \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\mathrm{E}}=\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{57 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-22}}\\
& \lambda=\frac{6.6 \times 3 \times 10^{-26}}{57 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-22}}\\
& \lambda=0.2171052 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ m}\\
& \lambda=217105.2 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{ m}\\
& \lambda=217105 Å \text{ (Approx.) }
\end{aligned}\)$

questions.solution: Clearly, $\mathrm{Y}=(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}) \cdot \mathrm{C}=(\mathrm{A} \cdot \mathrm{C})+(\mathrm{B} \cdot \mathrm{C})$ For $\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{A}=0, \mathrm{ B}=0 \& \mathrm{C}=1, & \mathrm{Y}=(0.1)+(0.1)=0 \\ \mathrm{ A}=1, \mathrm{ B}=0 \& \mathrm{C}=1, & \mathrm{Y}=(1.1)+(0.1)=1 \\ \mathrm{ A}=1, \mathrm{ B}=0 \& \mathrm{C}=0, & \mathrm{Y}=(0.1)+(0.0)=0 \\ \mathrm{ A}=0, \mathrm{ B}=1 \& \mathrm{C}=0, & \mathrm{Y}=(0.0)+(1.0)=0 \end{array} So, option (b) is correct.$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cylindrical capacitor has charge $\mathrm{Q}$ and length L. If both the charge and length of the capacitor are doubled, by keeping other parameters fixed, the energy stored in the capacitor
questions.solution:
The energy stored in a capacitor is given by
$E=\frac{Q^{2}}{2 C}$
Here, $C=\frac{2 \pi \in_{0} L}{\ln \left(\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}\right)}$, where
$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{L}=\text{ length of the cylindrical conductor } \\
\mathrm{R}_{1}=\text{ inner radius } \\
\mathrm{R}_{2}=\text{ outer radius } \\
\therefore \mathrm{C} \propto \mathrm{L} \Rightarrow \mathrm{E} \propto \frac{\mathrmQ^{2}}{\mathrm{~L}}
\end{array}
When both $Q$ and $L$ are doubled, by keeping other parameters fixed, the energy stored (E') becomes
\begin{array}{l}$E^{\prime} \propto $\frac{(2 Q)^{2}}{2 L}$\\
\propto $\frac{2 Q^{2}}{L}$\\
\therefore E^{\prime}=2 E
\end{array}
